verdict: The accepted version keeps every headline claim, including 'conclusively demonstrates', but adds substantial new evidence: polarization-resolved RIXS from a second facility at a different scattering angle, incident-energy dependence, a Γ–M vs Γ–K check, asymmetric fits with defined error bars and line-cut comparisons. It adds an explicit argument against an acoustic plasmon and qualifies the sum-rule claim about EELS. These look referee-driven and match old review items S2, S4, S6, S7, S8 and S11. The old review's sharpest objection, that the feature sits above the σ intra-band kinematic bound (S1), and the BSE convergence concern (S5) leave no trace in the main text. The supplement of the accepted version was not available, so some answers may sit there.

inferred_requests.title: Rule out an acoustic plasmon
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked whether the linearly dispersing feature could be the predicted σ–π acoustic plasmon rather than the continuum. The authors added a discussion and a supplementary section arguing the branch lies lower in energy for the measured geometry.

inferred_requests.title: Separate momentum dependence from geometry and polarization
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked for evidence that the shift is a q dispersion and not an orbital/matrix-element effect of rocking θin, e.g. other polarization, other scattering angle, Γ–K data. The authors added σ/π polarization data from a second facility at a different 2θ and a Γ–M vs Γ–K statement.

inferred_requests.title: Reconcile σ versus π attribution of the feature
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked which bands carry the feature, given that the BSE points to σ bands and the Lindhard decomposition shows comparable π weight. The authors reread Fig. 4c as σ at lower and π at higher energy and tied this to measured linear dichroism.

inferred_requests.title: Justify the fitting and the error bars
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely objected to symmetric Voigt fits of an asymmetric feature and to undefined error bars. The authors switched to asymmetric Voigt fits and defined error bars from the fit covariance.

inferred_requests.title: Check the Raman / resonant nature of the feature
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked for incident-energy dependence to show the feature is a constant-loss excitation and not fluorescence or an intermediate-state effect. The authors added an incident-energy dependence figure.

inferred_requests.title: Compare lineshapes, not just peak positions
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked for direct spectral comparisons between data, BSE and Lindhard, and comment on the asymmetry and width. The authors added line cuts and a paragraph on linewidth growing with q as expected for a continuum.

inferred_requests.title: Qualify the sum-rule argument and its generality
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely questioned the absolute statement that EELS cannot see the continuum and asked what is special about MgB2. The authors qualified the claim by energy-scale separation and added a discussion of why MgB2 works and where else it might.

inferred_requests.title: Place the result in the prior literature
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked for prior observations of inter-band and indirect intra-band particle-hole excitations and context for the higher-energy features. The authors added refs 2-4, 26-31 and a better description of ref 25; the novelty claims themselves were not narrowed.

inferred_requests.title: Reproducibility and sample description
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked for sample details and confirmation on more data. The authors added a growth description, TEY/TFY XAS and a second beamtime at BESSY II.

inferred_requests.title: Assign the 3 eV peak
inferred_requests.text: A referee may have asked about the higher-energy features, in particular a peak near 3 eV. The authors now assign it to a Landau-damped collective excitation seen in IXS and optics.

inferred_requests.title: Deposit data and code
inferred_requests.text: The weak data statement was likely flagged by the journal or a referee. Data are now deposited and code availability is stated.

inferred_requests.title: Clarify theory methods
inferred_requests.text: A referee may have asked for the k-mesh and the U calibration. The Methods now state a 512×512×512 grid and that U is calibrated against the 3 eV plasmon.

issue_status.reason: The velocity numbers and the ≈1.4 eVÅ vs 2 eVÅ statement are unchanged; no per-sheet v_F·q bounds or fit intercept are given.
σ/π polarization data, a second scattering angle (BESSY II, 2θ = 90°) and a Γ–M vs Γ–K statement were added; no (q∥, q⊥) table or recomputed χ along the real trajectory is visible in the main text.
The k-grid is now stated as 512×512×512, answering the mesh concern; the decomposition is still not defined band by band and no v_F·q bounds are shown.
An incident-energy dependence figure (Supp. Fig. S2) was added; no off-resonance or core-hole-off BSE test is mentioned.
No BSE convergence, smearing or functional tests are mentioned in the main text; the supplement was not available.
The acoustic plasmon is now discussed and argued to lie at lower energy for the probed geometry (Supp. Sec. F).
Fits are now asymmetric Voigt with covariance error bars and line cuts were added; no model-based lineshape or intensity scaling with q.
Fig. 4c is reread as σ lower, π higher, supported by measured dichroism; the BSE σ-only projection is kept.
The orbital weighting and U treatment are restated, not justified; the 'unaffected by U' tension is not discussed in the main text.
Line cuts (Supp. Fig. S6) were added, but the 'matches closely except at smaller q' wording and RPA-in-Fig.-3e gap remain.
The EELS claim is qualified by energy-scale separation; no material-specific loss-function number is given.
New references to prior inter-band and indirect intra-band observations were added; 'remained experimentally elusive' and 'no feature ... reported' are unchanged.
Growth description, TEY/TFY XAS and a second beamtime were added; no thickness, substrate, Tc or oxidation check.
Fig. 4a is now labelled χRPA in the caption; whether the Fig. 4c colours and axis changed cannot be read from the text layer.
Fig. 2b still reads q∥ = 0.016 Å−1 with no θin or q⊥.
A geometry figure (Supp. Fig. S3) may give θin; the Fig. 3 caption still gives no θin or normalization.
'below 0.2 Å−1' and 'up to ≈0.17 Å−1' are both kept.
No statement of T = 0 and δ next to Fig. 3d.
No comment on tight-binding deviations in the main text; the supplement was not available.
Broken S0 references in the main text are fixed; the supplement could not be checked.
Most typos fixed; 'Florescence' remains in the Fig. 2 caption.
Data deposited with a DOI and code availability stated.

unaddressed_major.title: Measured energies exceed the intra-band kinematic bound
unaddressed_major.why: No text touches the velocity numbers or the finite intercept; the only related addition (linewidth growth from kinematic widening) reads as an answer to a lineshape question, not this one. A rebuttal using the full 3D q is possible but leaves no trace.

unaddressed_major.title: BSE convergence at small q
unaddressed_major.why: BSE details were moved to the supplement, which we cannot see; a convergence note there or in the response letter is plausible, and the main text is silent.

unaddressed_major.title: Heuristic orbital weighting and role of U
unaddressed_major.why: The Methods restate the same cos^4/sin^4 weighting and U calibration without new justification, suggesting no referee pushed on it.
